extracted.intended_audience: PR professionals, communications teams, marketers, and anyone writing corporate or organizational press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing modern (2025) press releases that serve both journalists and AI-driven discovery systems; covers required components, format conventions, and optimization for distribution. Useful for PR/comms teams preparing news announcements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Should clearly state the news in a single short line, ideally under 100 characters. Combine with subhead and summary so those three elements can tell the story on their own.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subhead
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a brief expansion or hook after the headline; keep to one or two sentences and directly support or clarify the headline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 1–3 bullets to surface the most newsworthy facts or metrics for quick scanning by journalists and AI summarizers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opening Paragraph
rubrics_metrics.description: Answers what happened, when, where, why it matters (5Ws in 30 words).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The lead should succinctly cover the 5 Ws and fit within about 30 words so readers and AI can immediately understand the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Details Section
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide fuller context, background, data, and specifics here. Ensure the body adds depth without repeating the headline/subhead/summary verbatim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include at least one quote that adds perspective or insight rather than platitudes; quote attribution must include full name, title, and organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide high-quality assets and links (include press kit/media link URL). Include captions/alt text and ensure assets are easily accessible to media and discovery systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Call to Action
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tell the reader what to do next (e.g., visit a URL, register, contact someone). CTAs should be specific and actionable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tags/Keywords
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign topical tags and keywords to help human distribution lists and AI discovery/indexing; use entity-rich, distribution-relevant terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boilerplate
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A concise, up-to-date company description that provides essential background; ensure it is current and consistent with other corporate materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact Information
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include contact name, title, phone, email, and social handles. Provide responsive contacts so journalists can follow up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modern (2025) Audience Consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Structure the release for two audiences: human journalists and AI-driven discovery systems (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overview).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance readable prose for humans with structured, machine-friendly elements for AI: clear leads, metadata, and structured sections that enable both classic reporting and AI summarization.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI Search Optimization Elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Elements to improve AI discovery and summarization: schema markup, Q&A format sections, direct answer formatting, entity-rich content, citation-worthy data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement structured data (schema), include Q&A or FAQ-style sections and direct-answer blocks, use clear entity names and verifiable facts/citations to increase utility for AI overviews and extractive systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dateline (Release Date and Originating City)
rubrics_metrics.description: Release date and originating city (dateline) must appear in the release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place the dateline prominently at the top of the release (city and date) to signal timing and locale to journalists and archives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release Status Notice
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State whether the release is immediate or embargoed; if embargoed, provide the embargo date/time and any conditions for use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quote Attribution Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Quote attribution must include full name, title, organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every quoted block should be attributed with the speaker's full name, job title, and organization to ensure credibility and proper attribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media Link / Press Kit URL
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a media link or press kit URL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a clearly labeled link to downloadable assets, additional materials, or a press kit so journalists and content systems can access supporting resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Traditional End Marker
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conclude the release with a standard end marker so editors and systems recognize the end of the content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit Quality Rubric
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria indicating a high-quality press release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A press release is high quality if: all 11 elements are present; each element has substance (not filler); headline + subhead + summary tell the story alone; body adds depth without redundancy; quote adds insight, not platitudes; CTA is clear and actionable; boilerplate is current; contact is responsive.
